title: Big O Fundamentals
learningObjectives: Explain the topic and its assumptions.
Describe why it matters in solving programming problems.
Interpret a small example or trace.
Apply the idea to a new situation.

understand.concept: Big O describes an upper-bound growth category as input size increases, emphasizing dominant terms and ignoring constant factors. O(1), O(log n), O(n), O(n log n), and O(n²) are common growth classes. Big O is not an exact runtime.
understand.whyItMatters: Big O provides a shared language for scalability comparisons independent of a particular computer.
understand.analogy: A map scale describes how a journey changes with distance, not the exact time every traveler takes.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy simplifies the concept; real behavior depends on input, constraints, and implementation details.

explain.narrative: Define the task and assumptions, choose a method, trace it on a small example, then check edge cases. examples.title: Constant access
examples.explanation: Known-index access is modeled as O(1).

examples.title: Linear work
examples.code: let c=0; for(const v of [1,2,3,4])c++; console.log(c);
examples.explanation: A loop visits n elements: O(n).

examples.title: Quadratic work
examples.code: let c=0; for(let i=0;i<3;i++)for(let j=0;j<3;j++)c++; console.log(c);
examples.explanation: All pairs are visited: O(n squared).

examples.title: Dominant term
examples.explanation: For large n, n squared dominates n.

commonMistakes: Using a method without checking assumptions.
Confusing theoretical growth with exact runtime.
Failing to explain limitations or trade-offs.
